questions.subject: ENGLISH_LITERATURE
questions.topic: The digressive opening chapter of each book in Tom Jones
questions.learningObjective: Explain what the opening chapter of each book does for the novel.
questions.stem: Halfway through a design brief for a survey on narrative structure, the report must account for a convention in which every book of a comic novel in prose opens with a chapter that leaves the story behind, so explain what that chapter does.

answer.exemplar: Each of the eighteen books opens with a digressive chapter that suspends the narrative and turns to a general subject, argued in the mock-scholarly manner of an essay. The chapter comments on the story that follows, so the reader moves between the mock-heroic world of the plot and a world of literary and moral commentary, which is what makes the form a comic epic in prose.

questions.explanation: Every book opens with an essayistic digression, so the story is repeatedly interrupted by argument and reflection. Treating those chapters as padding misses the formal experiment at the heart of the work.
questions.hint: Ask what the chapter says besides telling the story.

answer.exemplar: The closing chapter has the travellers meet a schoolmaster and a priest whose lives are simple, useful and content, and Candide concludes that people should cultivate their own garden, meaning that useful labour and modest contentment are better than either philosophical optimism or cynical indulgence.

answer.exemplar: The closing chapter refuses both of the positions the tale has parodied. It rejects the claim that this is the best of all possible worlds, and it rejects the invitation to eat and drink and stop worrying, and it replaces them with the plain proposal that people should cultivate their garden, doing useful work on a small scale and expecting little.

questions.explanation: The closing chapter steers between the extremes the book has mocked, recommending modest labour and contentment. Reading it as restored optimism, or as despair, misses the middle position it occupies.

answer.exemplar: The opening chapters are written in the voice of a pretended scholar, and they often discuss the very difficulties the novel goes on to stage, such as how a writer should handle a good or bad protagonist and how a plot may be held back. questions.topic: Tristram Shandy printed in instalments and never finished
questions.learningObjective: Explain what the title of the unfinished novel signals about its subject.
questions.stem: The engineer's sketch notes for a library display ask about the title of an unfinished comic novel, and what it signals about the book's real subject.

options.text: It names the narrator, who tells a story he does not properly control or remember
It names the hero, who completes a long quest and returns home in the end
options.misconception: assumes the title figure finishes a quest the book never starts

options.text: It names the author, who signs his own work in a mock-scholarly manner
options.misconception: confuses the narrator's name with the writer's authorship

options.misconception: credits the publisher with a role the title does not give

questions.explanation: The title names the man who narrates, and the joke is that his own life is the story he handles worst, since his relatives supply the real subject. Reading the title as a quest or a signature misses the irony.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LITERATURE
questions.topic: Candide and the thesis its last chapter states
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a satirical tale ends almost without irony.
questions.stem: For a study group on tone, the engineer's sketch notes ask why a satirical tale ends almost without irony, and what that change accomplishes.

answer.exemplar: For most of the tale the narrator's tone is sardonic and every character is measured against the target of ridicule. In the final chapter the irony withdraws, and the people who appear are described plainly, with no wink at the reader. That withdrawal is what allows the recommendation to land, because if the closing pages still winked, the advice would be part of the joke instead of a serious settlement.

questions.explanation: The final chapter abandons the sardonic register that has governed the book, which is what lets its advice be taken seriously. Reading the ending as continued satire misses the tone shift that carries its force.
questions.hint: The wink is taken away on purpose.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LITERATURE
questions.topic: The digressive opening chapter of each book in Tom Jones
questions.learningObjective: Explain how the opening chapters instruct the reader.
questions.stem: The engineer's design brief for a teaching unit asks how the opening chapters instruct a reader, and what guidance they give about reading a comic novel in prose.

answer.exemplar: The opening chapters do not only entertain; they tell the reader what to expect and how to judge it, praising the form of the comic epic and warning against expecting refined ceremony at every turn of the story. They also set the rule that the writer will tell the truth as it appears, which lets the reader hold the book to a standard it has itself named in advance.

questions.explanation: The essays instruct readers in what to expect and how to judge the book, so they are a statement of method rather than a diversion. Reading them as mere entertainment misses the standards they set.
questions.hint: They tell you how to read what follows.

questions.learningObjective: State what the final chapter of Candide recommends and what it rejects.
questions.stem: Finally, an engineer's design brief lists the closing recommendation of a satirical tale whose last chapter is often quoted, so what does that chapter advise?

options.text: That everyone should seek the most brilliant fortune, since fortune rewards the bold
options.misconception: sets up fortune as the goal the ending actually rejects

options.text: That the world is perfect as made, so sorrow is always a sign of error
options.misconception: restates the optimism the chapter dismantles

options.text: That nothing matters, so the sensible course is to enjoy the present without hope
